title: Push notifications
summary: Your server sends a message to Apple's Push Notification service (APNs) with the device token; APNs delivers it to the device. Delivery is best-effort, so the app must still sync when opened.
body: **Flow in simple words:** (1) App asks the user for permission. (2) App registers with APNs and gets a **device token** (an address for this app on this device). (3) App sends the token to your backend. (4) Backend sends a JSON payload + token to APNs over HTTP/2, authenticated with a key (JWT). (5) APNs delivers to the device; iOS shows it.

**Payload basics:** `aps.alert` (title/body), `badge`, `sound`, `thread-id` (grouping), `category` (action buttons), custom keys for deep links. Headers: `apns-push-type` (alert, background, liveactivity...), `apns-priority`, `apns-collapse-id` (replace older notification), `apns-expiration`.
**Silent (background) push:** `content-available: 1`, no alert; wakes the app briefly to fetch data. Throttled by the system - not guaranteed.

**Notification Service Extension:** with `mutable-content: 1`, a small extension gets ~30 seconds to change the notification before display: download an image, decrypt end-to-end encrypted text. **Content Extension:** custom UI when the notification is expanded.
**Tokens change** (reinstall, restore, sometimes randomly): send the token to the server on every launch; server removes tokens APNs reports as unregistered (410).
**Handling taps:** `UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate.didReceive` → read custom data → deep link to the right screen. `willPresent` decides whether to show it while the app is in foreground.
**Other:** provisional authorization (quiet notifications without asking first), interruption levels (passive, active, time-sensitive, critical), Live Activities updated by push.
keyPoints: App → permission → device token → backend → APNs → device.
Best-effort delivery: always sync on app open.
Service extension modifies content (images, decryption) within ~30 s.
Silent pushes are throttled and not guaranteed.
Upload the token every launch; prune invalid tokens on the server.

code.caption: Register and handle taps

mistakes: Caching the device token and never re-uploading it.
Relying on push to deliver data reliably (e.g. chat messages) without syncing on open.
Asking for permission at first launch with no context (low opt-in).
followups: **How do you send rich media?** `mutable-content: 1` + Notification Service Extension downloads the media and attaches it.
**How do you measure delivery?** Include a message id; the service extension or app reports receipt; compare with sends.
**Sandbox vs production APNs?** Debug builds use the sandbox environment; TestFlight/App Store use production.
